answers.question: How many sparsity rates have at least one bar (either Per-Output or Per-Layer) with a perplexity value above 100?
answers.reasoning: On the log scale, only at 80% sparsity do both bars exceed 10² (~100): Per-Output is approximately 500 and Per-Layer approximately 900. All lower sparsity rates stay well below 100.

answers.question: What is the ratio of the Perplexity for Per-Layer to Per-Output at a sparsity rate of 70%?
answers.reasoning: At 70% sparsity, Per-Layer perplexity is approximately 40 and Per-Output is approximately 20, giving a ratio of 40 / 20 = 2.0.

answers.question: Rank the sparsity rates of 40%, 50%, and 60% in ascending order of the difference in perplexity between Per-Output and Per-Layer configurations.
answers.reasoning: Approximate Per-Layer minus Per-Output gaps are ~0.5 at 40%, ~0.5 at 50%, and ~1 at 60%, so the difference is smallest at 40% and largest at 60%.

answers.question: Does the gap between the Per-Layer and Per-Output configurations widen as sparsity rate increases, and if so, at which sparsity rates is this most pronounced?
answers.answer: Yes, the gap widens as sparsity rate increases, and this is most pronounced at 70% and 80% sparsity rates.
answers.reasoning: Per-Layer and Per-Output bars are nearly equal up to 60%, then diverge sharply at 70% (40 vs 20) and 80% (~900 vs ~500), where the Per-Layer penalty is largest.
